title: Warnings Ignored Before Fatal Kuwait Drone Strike, Army Whistleblower Claims
snippet: Army Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom alleges senior military leaders dismissed safety concerns at a Kuwait command post prior to an Iranian drone attack that killed six U.S. troops.
content:
A U.S. Army officer who survived a devastating Iranian drone attack in Kuwait has stepped forward as a whistleblower, alleging that senior military commanders ignored explicit warnings about vulnerable defenses prior to the fatal strike.

Army Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom filed a formal complaint with both the House and Senate Armed Services Committees on Friday. The complaint details critical security and logistical shortcomings at Port Shuaiba, a U.S. command post where six American service members were killed during the opening 24 hours of Operation Epic Fury. The March 1 strike stands as the single deadliest attack on U.S. forces in the conflict with Iran.

Lax Protections and Scarce Medical Resources

According to the complaint, military leadership repeatedly brushed aside concerns regarding inadequate fortifications at the site. Ramsbottom revealed that the facility was dangerously unprepared for combat operations, operating with no on-site physician, no fixed aid station, and just a single ambulance.

"I feel this is a tactical failure by the Army, our leadership, and myself — all the way down to my level," Ramsbottom said during an exclusive interview with 60 Minutes. "We just did not plan this well, and this needs to be a lesson that we learn."

Contrasting Accounts and Congressional Scrutiny

The whistleblower's account starkly contrasts public statements made by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth shortly after the attack. At a press conference, Hegseth insisted troops were well-protected and described the incoming drone as an unfortunate "squirter" that managed to strike a fortified tactical operations center.

However, eyewitness accounts alongside photos and videos obtained from the site depict a heavily exposed facility with minimal defenses. The revelation has sparked an immediate response on Capitol Hill.

Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, demanded Hegseth appear for a classified briefing and provide all internal force protection assessments for Port Shuaiba. Congressional Democrats have indicated they intend to launch broader inquiries into the military's handling of the conflict.

"The families of the six fallen servicemembers, the wounded survivors, and the American people deserve transparency and accountability," Blumenthal wrote in a letter sent to the Pentagon.

A spokesperson for the Department of Defense declined to comment on Ramsbottom's allegations or the defensive posture at Port Shuaiba.
